scope: Narrow successor response to the exact TrustedRequestContext v2 rejection only. designResponse.authorityRoot: Each TrustedHostRequestAuthorityV3 instance is an independent root. The selected host authority alone owns an out-of-band ledger state mapping each canonical exactly-once reserved RequestId to one exact context object.
designResponse.contextShape: TrustedRequestContextV3 has empty slots and exposes no RequestId, authority, gate, registry, token, mint helper, or projection helper. Its only usable provenance fact is exact object identity when presented back to the selected authority.
designResponse.admissionTransaction: begin validates kind, prior-context absence, canonical representation, and uniqueness; constructs the context; builds a complete next RequestId-to-(count=1, exact object) state; then replaces the authority state once. This is a single-process model only, not durable atomicity evidence.
designResponse.projection: TrustedHostRequestAuthorityV3.request_id consults only its own state, accepts no caller registry/authority arguments, requires exact context type and exact object identity, requires one match and reservation count exactly one, and returns the canonical bound key.
designResponse.authorityIsolation: A context valid under a separately created authority rejects under the selected authority. Creating an equivalent fresh authority therefore cannot recreate the v2 self-authenticating gate bypass.
designResponse.ordinaryAttackClosure: Direct allocation, direct no-ingress allocation, populated substitute registry, second authority, duplicate claim, unreserved claim, context authority leak, slot injection, raw/JSON/lookalike values, copy/deepcopy/pickle, and six distinct component construction routes all reject without selected-authority state change.
designResponse.modelBoundary: This Python executable is a trusted-host API/provenance model, not a same-process security sandbox. Arbitrary inspection or mutation of Python private state, process-memory writes, and debugger compromise remain outside claim. Those powers are not used by the retained v2 attacks. Production Rust privacy/capability ownership remains required.

findingDispositions.response: The exact source helper remains hash-before-compile/exec. Unlike v2's authored regression, both v3 cache and wrong-hash probes invoke the actual _exec_pinned_source helper through its isolated-root test parameter. A timestamp-valid malicious pyc cannot write its marker; a wrong source hash refuses before source side effects.
V2's gate-based repair was rejected and is not defended. V3 moves authenticity entirely out of the fieldless context and into the selected authority's exact reservation-to-object binding.

No gate, context-supplied authority, module registry, or module mint helper remains. Projection is selected-authority-owned and accepts only the exact object already bound in that authority's exactly-once reservation state.

TRC3-NEG-22 constructs a nonempty canonical RequestId-to-(count=1, exact forged object) registry and supplies it to projection; the parameter is rejected and selected state remains exact. TRC3-NEG-21 additionally uses a genuinely populated second authority.

The v3 oracle is structural and behavioral: context fields/methods, authority-state write owners, global authority/context instances, legacy definitions, and independently rooted mint behavior are inspected. The decisive behavioral result is that a fresh equivalent authority's valid context rejects under the selected authority.

Caller, sink, provider, stage, profile, and projection adapter now use six distinct retained route functions with six distinct code objects; each directly allocates an exact-type object and rejects without state change.
TRC3-ADV-01 and TRC3-ADV-02 call the actual normal-path _exec_pinned_source helper; no duplicated hash/compile/exec implementation is used by the regression.
